subject: Pricing exhibit: packaging conversion and cap/floor reconciliation (Clarion Data)
messages:
From: Amir Sayeed <amir.s@clariondata.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clariondata.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exhibit C - pricing mapping questions

Kimberly —

Thanks for sending the draft. Our legal and procurement teams flagged a couple of substantive issues in Exhibit C that block Countersign for Clarion:

1) Cap/floor treatment when customers change packaging (e.g., moving from Standard Pack to Bulk Pack). The current text references a "committed band" but does not define how caps/floors translate across packaging boundaries. We need a clear mapping or a fallback rule.

2) True-up mechanics are ambiguous. Exhibit C references a "quarterly reconciliation" but lacks the formula and an example. Our auditors need an explicit calc (including token-to-unit conversion and rounding rules).

3) Anchor language: the "anchoring" sentence in 4.a can be read to let the vendor reclassify consumption into different fee buckets mid-quarter. We can't accept a clause that permits retroactive repackaging without an objective rule.

I've attached our marked-up Exhibit C (Clarion_ExhibitC_Redline.pdf). For speed, could you provide:
- A redline showing: (a) a mapping table for package conversions OR (b) fallback logic;
- A 1-page worked example for the true-up calc;
- A note on whether Redwood's billing system supports prorated packaging changes mid-cycle.

Happy to hop on a short call if that's easier — our procurement lead is available tomorrow morning.

Best,
Amir Sayeed
Senior Counsel, Clarion Data
attachments: Clarion_ExhibitC_Redline.pdf

Subject: Fwd: Clarion redline — quick triage

Internal — forwarding Clarion's redline. Key asks summarized below (keeping it short so we can align before I respond):

- Clarion wants a deterministic mapping for package changes (cap/floor translation) or a strict fallback rule.
- They need an explicit true-up formula and a worked example.
- They are worried about any language that allows retroactive reclassification of usage into higher fee bands.

Options I think we can offer:
A) Explicit mapping table + worked example in Exhibit C. Table shows token-to-CU factor per package and an example conversion.
B) Fallback rule: if packaging changes mid-quarter, prorate by active days and apply quarterly true-up.

Operational constraints: do we support prorated packaging changes today? Karthik, can you confirm whether billing emits pro-rated invoices and whether our orderform schema can capture a token-to-CU factor per line item?

Laura — if we go with (B) I'd propose inserting a short, objective formula into 4.a and limiting retroactivity to cases where both parties agree to a package reclassification (or when we detect a clear billing misclassification).

I've attached triage notes (kp_triage_notes.txt). Will hold off replying to Clarion until we align.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
attachments: kp_triage_notes.txt

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarion redline — quick triage

Kimberly / Laura —

Quick ops perspective: we can support prorated packaging changes and the billing system can emit pro rata lines; that will drive a slightly higher implementation cost but it's doable. Recommended approach below:

Proposal (concise):
- Insert a deterministic formula in Exhibit C, paragraph 4.a:
  Committed Units (CU) for any quarter = floor(Committed_Tokens / Token_to_CU_Factor) where Token_to_CU_Factor is defined per package in Table 1. If Customer changes package mid-quarter, CU will be prorated by active days in each package (see worked example).

- Worked example (include in Exhibit C appendix):
  Example: Customer committed 900,000 tokens = 9,000 CU under Standard Pack (factor = 100 tokens/CU). On day 31 of the quarter they move to Bulk Pack (factor = 250 tokens/CU). CU calculation = floor((900,000 * 30/90) / 100) + floor((900,000 * 60/90) / 250) = 3,000 + 2,400 = 5,400 CU. Quarterly true-up will compare actual CU consumption to committed CU and settle over/under by contract tier pricing.

- On retroactive reclassification: we should keep our standard protection — no retroactive up-classing unless there is evidence of meter error or mutual agreement. We can concede waiving overage for the first billing period after a packaging change (goodwill) to help Clarion sign.

I attached a quick calc sheet (billing_calc.xlsx) with the formulas. From an implementation standpoint, ops needs a signed orderform that includes the Table 1 mapping and the Token_to_CU_Factor recorded on the order line.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call with Clarion to walk through the numbers if helpful.

thanks,
Karthik
Billing & Platform Operations
attachments: billing_calc.xlsx

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Amir Sayeed <amir.s@clariondata.com>

Subject: Re: Exhibit C - pricing mapping questions

Amir —

Thanks for the clear redline and the call offer. We reviewed internally and attached a focused redline that addresses your three asks: Redline_ExhibitC_Clarion_kp.docx. Summary of the changes we made:

- Inserted Table 1 (Token_to_CU_Factor) into Exhibit C and a short definition for "Committed Unit (CU)".
- Added a deterministic formula and a concise worked example in an appendix (the example matches the math Karthik sent).
- Clarified the anchor language in 4.a: we will not retroactively up-classify usage absent meter error or mutual written agreement. We can include a concession: waive overage charges for the first invoice cycle after an agreed packaging change (one-time goodwill credit).

Quick answers to your specific questions:
- Redline: attached.
- Worked example: included in the appendix (see page 3 of the redline).
- Billing support for prorate: yes — we support prorated packaging changes and will capture Token_to_CU_Factor at order time as a line-item attribute.

If this looks acceptable, we can either:
1) Get a confirmatory reply ("Accepted as redlined") and prepare an orderform with Table 1 populated, or
2) Schedule a short 20-minute call tomorrow AM to walk through the math and finalize language.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
